# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v40)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod attendance); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); **1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion and Bombarda's restaurant dinner); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop with Thénardier family and Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's Champmathieu revelation; Valjean's acute crisis continuing through late night into early morning and through entire journey to Arras); 1862 (narrative reflection on changed Paris)**; present day (spring transitioning to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); 1795 (Jean Valjean's theft at Faverolles and trial)
- Primary locations: M. sur M. (industrial center, upper and lower town divisions, factory, hospital, infirmary for workmen, schools, dispensary, free school for infants, industrial exhibition venue, officers' café, police station, parsonage); Montfermeil (Thénardier cook-shop, Boulanger Lane); Arras (trial site); Hesdin (crossroad location); England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford harbor towns, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby); Secondary locations: San Francisco, New York, Eastern Prussia, Germany, Hamburgh, Paris, Italy, Durance, Château-Arnoux, Senez, Briançon, Aix, Draguignan, Embrun, Chastelar, Arche, Barcelonette, Jauziers, Tuiles, Joug-de-l'Aigle, Ubaye, Ubayette, Ollioules, Nice, Piédmont, Couloubrieux, Cannes, Rue Cassette, Elmhaven, Staveford, Grenoble, Bras d'Asse, Escoublon, Grasse, Franche-Comté, Pontarlier, Lods, Châtillon, Audincourt, Beure, Faverolles, Brie, Tottlingen, Toulon, Quenford, Ravenmere, Basses-Alpes, Latin Quarter Paris, Mount Sainte-Geneviève, Toulouse, Cahors, Limoges, Montauban, Naples, Saint-Cloud, Fécamp, Vanvres, Issy, Passy, l'Étoile, Champs-Élysées, Rue de Rivoli, Delorme Alley, Place de la Concorde, Place Louis XV, Avenue de Neuilly, Tuileries, Marigny square, Odéon, Luxembourg, Rue Madame, Allée de l'Observatoire, Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas, Coural das Freiras vineyard, Madeira, Rue Saint-Antoine Paris, Pont-à-Mousson, Ailly-le-Haut-Clocher, Rue Saint-Saulve, Rue Montre-de-Champigny, Rue Guibourg, Rue du Garraud-Blanc, Marines near Pontoise, D——, Manosque, Sisteron, Hautes-Alpes, Lower Boulonnais, Romainville (little grove near Paris where young lovers pluck lilacs in April; also inscription on old clock for sale)
- **Recurring atmospheric descriptions**: Evening at cook-shop; bell for vespers rings thinly; children chase hoop shrieking; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; cart with turnips creaks past well; gulls quarrel over fish heads; dog barks then goes quiet; frost silvered hedges overnight; light went early; road rutted and puddled after thaw; wind off water with salt and tar smell; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; rain threatening since morning but held off

## Main Characters and Relationships

**Jean Valjean / Father Madeleine—JOURNEY TO ARRAS UNDERWAY**
- **Background**: Poor peasant of Brie; tree-pruner at Faverolles. At 25-26 (1795): condemned to five years galleys for stealing loaf; sentence extended to nineteen years total for four escape attempts. Toulon (19 years): became number 24,601; aged 40, learned to read, write, cipher. Released with yellow passport; worked at Grasse before arriving D——, October 1815.
- **October 1815 transformation**: Medium stature, robust, ~46 years old; burned face. Bishop's supper: mystical vision where conscience weighed Bishop against Valjean; Bishop grew resplendent while Valjean vanished; only radiance remained. Wept; perceived Satan by light of Paradise. Crisis marked decisive transformation through divine confrontation with virtue's radiance.
- **Reinvention and charitable works (late 1815 onward)**: Disappeared, sold Bishop's silver (reserved candlesticks), arrived M. sur M. as Father Madeleine. Fire incident: saved two children, gendarmes forgot passport. Substituted gum-lac for resin using sheet-iron slides. Within three years: became rich (630,000-640,000 francs with Laffitte), enriched town. Founded six hospital beds, two schools, infant school, fund for old/infirm workmen, free dispensary, infirmary for workmen with sisters of charity. 1819: Refused mayoral appointment and chevalier. 1820: Accepted mayoralty after questioning old woman's anger, irritated into compliance.
- **Personal character (1820-1821)**: Simple, gray hair, serious eye, sunburned, thoughtful. Wore wide-brimmed hat, long coat buttoned to chin. Took meals alone with open book; well-selected library; polished, gentle language; prodigiously strong; pockets full going out, empty returning; concealed good actions.
- **January 1823 Fantine crisis**: Upon arrest news, arrived at police station. Fantine spit in his face. Madeleine calmly wiped face, ordered release. Promised: "I will pay your debts, I will send for your child... You have never ceased to be virtuous and holy in the sight of God."
- **SUPREME CRISIS TO DECISION (Late January 1823, night through early morning to current journey)**:
  - **Internal voice and despair**: Conscience's external voice condemned inaction as wretch's choice, detailing Champmathieu's impending doom while Valjean remains honored mayor. Voice declared blessings would turn to maledictions. Recognized both resolutions (self-preservation vs. self-denunciation) equally fatal; perceived cosmic fatality. Name Romainville and song fragment recurred. Torment unchained afresh from which he had barely escaped.
  - **Final paralysis and decision threshold**: All reasoning sketched by meditation quivered into smoke. Recognized that regardless of choice, something in him must die; he was entering sepulchre either way; passing through dual death agony. Compared his agony to Christ's Gethsemane agony—dreadful cup dripping darkness, overflowing shadows.
  - **Dream/nightmare record (CLAIM)**: Experienced painful, heart-rending nightmare unrelated to situation. **Narrative possesses written record in Valjean's own handwriting which he bequeathed.** Dream depicted plain with no trees; nude man color of ashes on earth-colored horse, bald with visible veins, holding supple iron-heavy vine-like switch; horseman passed silently. Valjean entered deserted town—streets, doors, chambers empty. Behind each angle stood silent watchers, only one visible at time. Great crowd overtook him—all men seen before, earthen-hued faces, moving silently faster. Crowd surrounded him. Vision interrupted by carriage sounds; distinguished tilbury with lanterns; recognized white horse hoofs on pavement.
  - **Post-crisis action (Excerpt 338-344)**: **DECISION MADE**: Hired Scaufflaire's tilbury and white horse; departed M. sur M. night of January 1823 collision with descending post-wagon at town corner. Drove at full gallop, pursued his road. Whither going? He could not have told. Why hastening? Did not know. Drove at random, straight ahead—possibly Arras, possibly elsewhere. At times conscious and shuddered. Plunged into night as into gulf. Something urged him forward; something drew him on. **INTERNAL RATIONALIZATION**: When hired cabriolet, repeated to himself: no reason not to see with own eyes, judge for himself—prudent, must know what takes place, no decision without observation; one makes mountains from distance; when seen Champmathieu (a wretch), conscience probably relieved allowing him to galleys in his stead; Javert would be there and old convicts (Brevet, Chenildieu, Cochepaille) would not recognize him; Javert a hundred leagues from suspecting truth; all conjectures fixed on Champmathieu, nothing so headstrong as suppositions; no danger accordingly.
  - **Journey progression (Excerpt 340-344)**: At daybreak, open country; M. sur M. lay far behind. Watched horizon grow white; stared at chilly figures of winter's dawn without seeing them. Morning spectres passed before eyes unperceived; black silhouettes of trees and hills added gloomy, sinister quality to violent state of his soul. Horse (small Boulonnais race—too much head, too much belly, not enough neck/shoulders, but broad chest, large crupper, thin fine legs, solid hoofs—homely, robust, healthy) had travelled five leagues in two hours, not a drop sweat on loins. **DELAY AT HESDIN**: Conversation with wheelwright about obtaining fresh horses. Wheelwright offered old calash under shed belonging to bourgeois, requiring two horses, barely functional; post-horses would require three-four hours delay at every relay; season for ploughing beginning; heavy teams required everywhere; many hills to ascend. **INTERPRETATION OF OBSTACLE**: Interpreted broken tilbury wheel and delay as Providence intervening, stopping him on road. Had not yielded to first summons; made every possible effort to continue journey; loyally exhausted all means; deterred neither by season, fatigue, nor expense; nothing to reproach himself. If went no further, no fault of his; concern no longer his; act of Providence, not his conscience. **PUBLIC REVELATION**: Conversation occurred in street, not inn chamber, attracting crowd of spectators. Young lad detached from group and ran off. **FURTHER DELAY**: Lost great deal of time at Hesdin; wanted to make it good. Little horse courageous but month was February, roads bad after rain; no longer tilbury—cart very heavy, many ascents. **CONTEMPLATION DURING JOURNEY**: Watched trees, thatched roofs, tilled fields, landscape vanishing; contemplation sometimes suffices soul, almost relieves thought. Melancholy and profound to see thousand objects first and last time. Travel is birth and death at every instant. In vaguest region of mind, perhaps made comparisons between shifting horizon and human existence: all life's things perpetually flee before us; dark and bright intervals intermingled; after dazzling moment, eclipse; we look, hasten, stretch hands to grasp passing; each event a turn in road; all at once old; feel shock; all black; distinguish obscure door; gloomy horse of life, drawing us, halts; see veiled unknown person unharnessing amid shadows.

**Javert** (Police Inspector at M. sur M.)
- **Origin and psychology**: Born in prison; mother fortune-teller, father in galleys. Conscious of rigidity, regularity, probity with inexpressible hatred for bohemians. Entered police; succeeded. Age 40, appointed inspector at M. sur M. One of few escaping "contagion" of respect for Madeleine; possessed "bestial instinct" creating imperious antipathies.
- **Physical appearance**: Flat nose, enormous whiskers, rare terrible laugh, savage fold around nose, little skull with great jaw, hair concealing forehead, permanent central frown, obscure gaze, pursed terrible mouth, air of ferocious command.
- **Recognition and denunciation (late January 1823)**: **CLAIM/FACT**: Believes Madeleine is Jean Valjean, convict whom he knew at Toulon. **Evidence**: Resemblance; inquiries at Faverolles; strength; adventure with Fauchelevent; marksmanship; leg drag. **ACTION**: Impelled by wrath, denunciated Madeleine to Prefecture. **CLAIM about Valjean**: After leaving galleys, robbed bishop, committed theft with violence on public highway against little Savoyard; disappeared eight years ago.
- **Confrontation with Madeleine (late January 1823)**: Confronted Madeleine with grave, supplicating words. Informed of arrest of old fellow named Father Champmathieu near Ailly-le-Haut-Clocher, "very wretched creature," arrested last autumn for cider apple theft.
- **Reaction to dismissal**: Madeleine abruptly dismissed Javert's account, dispatching him on multiple minor tasks to isolate him during crisis.
- **Post-1820 response to mayoral authority**: Upon seeing Madeleine in mayoral scarf, felt shudder watch-dog might smelling wolf in master's clothes. From that time, avoided him; when service demanded meeting, addressed him with profound respect.
- **January 1823 street incident with Fantine**: Arrested Fantine following altercation with dandy. Judged crime serious: prostitute attempted assault on citizen. Upon Madeleine's arrival and command for release, experienced "intoxication of amazement." **Unspoken hideous comparison formed** concerning woman and mayor's relationship. When Madeleine explained townsman was wrong, **felt compelled to oppose mayor for first time in his life**. **Command to release immediately obeyed**, demonstrating absolute authority superseding police discretion.

**Fantine—MYSTICAL REDEMPTION IN CONSUMPTION**
- **1817 status**: Beautiful, sunny hair, youngest grisette, radiant, perfumed.
- **1817 abandonment**: Félix Tholomyès departed via Toulouse diligence; left her dazzled and alone.
- **1818 spring (Montfermeil)**: Transformed, difficult to recognize. Pale, weary, sickly; golden hair concealed beneath ugly tight cap; eyes not dry long. Placed child with Thénardiers; paid initial fee (50-57 francs).
- **Post-dismissal catastrophe (1818-1823)**: No one hired her. Learned indigence. Winter cycle: short days, no warmth, light. Creditors harassed. Thénardiers fabricated medical claims threatening Cosette's death. Sacrificed hair. By end, resigned, marble-like indifference.
- **January 1823 street incident and arrest**: Snowy evening, dandy put snow down her back. Fantine struck out with feet and fists, bareheaded, howling, minus hair and teeth, livid with wrath. Officers applauded. Javert dragged her to police station.
- **At station**: Spoke rent in twain, shaken with sobs, blinded with tears. **"Great sorrow is a divine and terrible ray, which transfigures the unhappy. At that moment Fantine had become beautiful once more."** Kissed Javert's coat tenderly pleading. Upon learning Madeleine present, rose like spectre, spit in his face. Madeleine calmly wiped face and ordered release.
- **Madeleine's redemptive promise**: "I will pay your debts, I will send for your child... You have never ceased to be virtuous and holy in the sight of God."
- **Following day**: Madeleine gazing at crucifix with look full of pity, anguish, supplication. Addressed her: "You have suffered much, poor mother... this hell from which you have just emerged is the first form of heaven. It was necessary to begin there."
- **Medical condition (post-January 1823)**: Sisters initially received with repugnance; within days disarmed through humble, gentle speech; motherhood provoked tenderness. Amid fever, spoke: "I have been a sinner; but when I have my child beside me, it will be a sign that God has pardoned me... Cosette is an angel." Did not recover health; condition became more grave week by week. Snow applied to bare skin caused sudden perspiration suppression, developing malady. **Consumption/tuberculosis progressing; Madeleine informed "is losing ground fast."**

**Cosette** (Age ~7-8 in 1823)
- **Appearance at arrival (1818 spring, age 2-3)**: Most divine creature; coquettish dress with fine linen cap, Valenciennes lace; admirably rosy and healthy; great blue eyes with magnificent lashes.
- **Treatment by Thénardiers (post-1818)**: After money spent, treated as charity case. Dressed in cast-off petticoats; fed on scraps; made to run errands, sweep, wash dishes, carry burdens. Called the _Lark_ in neighborhood. Sweet, feeble being, incessantly punished, scolded, ill-used, beaten.
- **Thénardier's obstruction (late January 1823 onward — PLAN)**: Does not "let go of the child"; Cosette not quite well enough to take journey in winter. Petty but pressing debts remain in neighborhood.

**Thénardier** (Cook-shop keeper at Montfermeil)
- **Financial scheme**: Initial payment (50-57 francs); first six months seven francs monthly; then twelve; then fifteen. Fantine became irregular.
- **Fabricated medical claims (1818-1823)**: Wrote constantly claiming Cosette ill with miliary fever requiring expensive drugs; threatened Cosette's death if payments not sent within week.
- **Billing (January 1823)**: Presented bill for five hundred-plus francs to Madeleine. Two items over three hundred francs—one for doctor, one for apothecary attending Éponine and Azelma through long illnesses. Cosette had not been ill; "trifling substitution of names." Wrote at foot "Received on account, three hundred francs."

**Minor Characters**
- **Monsieur Scaufflaire**: Fleming, horse-trader of M. sur M. Possesses small white horse from Lower Boulonnais; gentle, harnessed to tilbury. **Rented carriage and white horse to Madeleine for journey to Arras.**
- **Sisters Perpétue and Simplice**: Sisters of Charity at infirmary.
- **Dandy / Monsieur Bamatabois**: Elector, proprietor of handsome three-story house. Put snow down Fantine's back; engaged in altercation; officers applauded.
- **Wheelwright at Hesdin**: Offered old calash and advised post-horse relay system; conversation with Valjean overheard by crowd, including young lad who ran off.
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: Owner of jade mirror mentioned in narrative.
- **Ulrald Corrford**: Worked as mason; possessed silver flute.
- **Marald Corrford**: Worked as cooper.
- **Nylia Corrford**: Worked as fisher; born in Quenford.
- **Yera Stenworth**: Shepherd; born in Ravenmere.
- **Lurald Stenworth ("Lame Lurald")**: Weaver.
- **Yedan Corrford**: Tanner; born at Dunstead.
- **Monsieur Laffitte**: Banker, Rue d'Artois, Paris (holds Madeleine's accounts).

## Themes
- **Moral crisis as cosmic warfare**: Conscience's external voice condemning silence; dual paths through spiritual sepulchre; comparison to Christ's Gethsemane agony; inability to choose without spiritual death
- **Providence and interpretation**: Valjean interprets broken tilbury wheel as Providence intervening to stop him; rationalizes delay as redemptive obstacle; transforms obstacle into divine sign
- **Human contemplation and mortality**: Landscape meditation on human existence; travel as birth and death at every instant; all life's things perpetually flee before us; gloomy horse of life that draws then halts; unveiling of unknown person unharnessing amid shadows
- **Authority hierarchy crisis**: Mayoral command supersedes police discretion; Javert's absolute authority confronted by Madeleine's mercy
- **Divine pardon through maternal mysticism**: Fantine's consumption-ridden body becoming site of spiritual redemption; anticipated reunion with Cosette as manifestation of divine pardon
- **Public revelation and rumor**: Wheelwright's street conversation overheard; young lad runs off—knowledge spreading in town concerning Valjean's departure and destination
